Functions that need the         host's public ledger (`shield`/`unshield`/mint) stay in the host; everything purely         confidential lives here.","errors":{"FHERC20InvalidReceiver(address)":[{"details":"The given receiver `receiver` is invalid for transfers."}],"SafeCastOverflowedUintDowncast(uint8,uint256)":[{"details":"Value doesn't fit in an uint of `bits` size."}]},"kind":"dev","methods":{"autoShield(address,address,uint256)":{"details":"Shield `amount` (public base units, e.g. just minted by a wrap) into `to`'s      confidential balance when the {IMintModePolicy} resolves PRIVATE for `to`.      Best-effort BY DESIGN \u2014 auto-shielding is sugar on top of the calling flow      (typically a wrap, on the money path) and must never change its success      envelope, so every non-shieldable case degrades to \"leave the mint public\"      instead of reverting:        - `mintModes == address(0)`: feature disabled at deployment;        - policy call reverts: fail-open to PUBLIC;        - sub-precision amount (`amount < rate`): nothing to shield \u2014 and as with          {shield}, the `amount % rate` remainder always stays public;        - amount exceeds the euint64 domain: the user can shield in parts.      The pre-checks guarantee the strict {shieldTo} cannot revert. No reentrancy      surface beyond {shield}'s own: the ledger leg is a self-call into the host's      `_transfer` and the FHE ops call the trusted task manager."},"createClaim(address,bytes32)":{"details":"Records a pending unshield claim keyed by a UNIQUE per-claimant id, not by the ciphertext handle. CoFHE handles are content-addressed (a pure function of the operation lineage, with no per-caller or per-call salt), so two unshields of an identical burned-amount lineage produce the SAME handle; keying claims by that handle would let a second unshield overwrite the first claimant's record and redirect their payout. The handle is retained as `ctHash` to bind the decryption proof in {handleClaim}."},"grantObserverPast(uint256[])":{"details":"Body of the hosts' `grantObserverPast` (the host keeps only its      access-control gate): grant the configured observer FHE access to      historical handles the host owns."},"grantPast(address,uint256[])":{"details":"Grant `observer` FHE access to historical ciphertext handles the host already owns (`allowThis`'d) \u2014 past transfer amounts (from {ConfidentialTransfer} events) and/or current balance handles (from `confidentialBalanceOf`). Closes the forward-only gap of the observer hook in `update()`. Runs under delegatecall, so `FHE.allow` executes as the host token, which holds permanent ACL on every handle it created. NOTE: on real CoFHE, a ctHash the host never owned reverts the whole call \u2014 the off-chain indexer must supply only this token's handles."},"reassignClaim(bytes32,address)":{"details":"Re-points an UNSETTLED claim at `newTo`, keeping its id, and moves it between the two `_userClaims` sets. Pure bookkeeping: authorization is the host's job (see {FHERC20WrapperClaims-reassignClaim}), which is the only caller that knows the operator rules."},"setObserver(address)":{"details":"Body of the hosts' `setObserver` (the host keeps only its access-control      gate): a bare storage write plus the event."},"shieldTo(address,uint256)":{"details":"The shield primitive with an explicit recipient: moves `to`'s public tokens      into the pool and credits `to`'s confidential balance. Strict like {shield}      always was (dust-only amounts and uint64 overflow revert). `to`-addressed so      flows where `msg.sender` is NOT the account being shielded (e.g. a wrap,      where `msg.sender` is the SwapFacility) can use it via {autoShield}."},"syncConfidentialTotalSupply()":{"details":"Materializes the confidential total supply (pool balance / conversion rate) as a REGISTERED ciphertext handle. Runs inside every pool-balance-changing operation (shield / claim / confidential mint \u2014 NOT unshield: the pool keeps custody until the claim settles, so the supply still counts pending claims, same as the pool balance itself). The plaintext is derived from public state, so a trivial encryption suffices \u2014 no FHE arithmetic. `allowPublic` is deliberate: the value was never secret (anyone can read the pool's public balance), and the global ACL grant covers EVERY account \u2014 decryption by any consumer, use in other contracts' FHE ops, and the host's own future access (so no `allowThis` needed: `isAllowed` = transient \u2228 persisted \u2228 global)."},"update(address,address,bytes32)":{"details":"Saturating decrease on `from`, increase on `to`, ACL grants, indicator mirror, and the {ConfidentialTransfer} log.
